thread:
zhen: quick topic - re: multi-objective routing. we keep hitting edge cases where cost vs latency vs regional affinity fight each other. want to propose a small DSL addition + runtime normalization change.
leo: short version: bring policy-level utility functions so operators can express tradeoffs, runtime still enforces stability & lower-overhead evaluation.
anya: utility functions are powerful but risky. we need strong guardrails: bounded coefficients, monotonicity checks, and a deterministic tie-break.
sophia: also consider adding a "soft_constraint" primitive (expressed as penalty if violated) rather than hard excludes. helps keep availability when constraints are slightly missed.
zhen: exactly. idea: policy DSL additions: 1) utility = sum_i (w_i * normalized(metric_i)) 2) soft_constraint(metric, threshold, penalty) 3) tag_boost(tag, bonus). runtime will: normalize metrics to [0,1], apply monotonic transforms, then compute utility.
leo: normalization note: metrics have different units. runtime will maintain a rolling baseline per metric (p50/p95) and map raw -> normalized via clamp((raw - min)/(max-min)). config can specify transform: linear/log.
anya: we should provide built-in presets: cost-focused, latency-focused, balanced. don't require authors to craft transforms.
sophia: operational concern: runtime has to evaluate this at 10s of thousands qps. keep evaluation O(1) per candidate and cache candidate features for ttl. we should restrict DSL to simple arithmetic and builtins, no loops.
zhen: agreed. limited expression language (affine combos, max/min, exp/log). whitelist functions. compile policies to an internal bytecode and validate at load time.
leo: migration story: old policies using weight-based selectors remain supported. new utility-based policies can be author opt-in per tenant. conversion helper: weight -> utility with a simple mapping. but warn operators about non-linear effects.
anya: tie-break and stability: propose stable-sort by utility, but add a hysteresis layer: if previous chosen adapter remains within delta_utility (configurable), keep it to avoid routing churn. also prefer adapters with higher confidence tag when similar.
sophia: runbook: if utility calc fails for a candidate (e.g., missing metrics), runtime should apply a conservative penalty and mark candidate as degraded rather than dropping. that avoids blackholing.
zhen: sample DSL snippet for RFC (draft):
```
policy {
  objective {
    normalize: { cost: { method: "log", p50: true }, latency: { method: "linear" } }
    utility: "-1.0*cost + -0.6*latency + 0.8*confidence + tag_boost(region:eu, 0.2)"
  }
  soft_constraint { metric: "p95_latency", threshold_ms: 250, penalty: 0.75 }
}
```
leo: nice. two questions: 1) how do adapters surface metrics? 2) how do we keep adapters cheap?
anya: adapters return a small feature map on hot path: {cost_micros, latency_p50_ms, p95_ms?, confidence, tags, version, ttl}. nothing heavy. runtime computes normalized values from those and from global baselines. cache entries per candidate keyed by adapter_id+version.
sophia: TTL floor again: enforce min_ttl=3s and max_ttl=60s for runtime cache, configurable per deployment. also emit cache_hit metrics.
zhen: telemetry: emit polyrouting.policy.utility{policy_id,adapter_id,tenant,region} and polyrouting.policy.choice_delta to help evaluate churn. also emit degraded_count and soft_constraint_violations.
leo: simulation: policy-sim needs enhancement to replay recorded adapter features and calculate utility deltas and churn. we should add a canary-sim mode that replays live traces and compares route sets.
anya: rollout: feature flag per-tenant + size-limited canary. start with internal tenants and low-traffic customers. watch cost, p99 latency, and choice-stability metric. if choice-stability drops > 5% or p99 increases > 30ms or cost-per-token increases > 10% for 30m, auto-disable for that tenant.
sophia: tests: 1) DSL unit tests parsing & fuzzing. 2) compiled bytecode validator. 3) integration in policy-sim with recorded traces and golden outputs. 4) perf bench for hot-path evaluation at target qps.
zhen: docs: clear examples for common objectives (latency-first, cost-first, geo-affinity), migration guide from weight -> utility, and adapter spec for feature map.
leo: naming: use polyrouting.multiobj.* metric prefix. include adapter_version in all logs. tag metrics with policy_id for correlation.
anya: edge-case: when baselines shift fast (e.g., a region warms up), normalization ranges may be stale and cause wild swings. propose smoothing window and a fallback static range if variance > threshold.
sophia: ops: schedule a 6h soak on internal infra before any external canary. policy-bot: please schedule.
policy-bot: scheduled soak window: 2026-04-02T01:00:00Z -> 2026-04-02T07:00:00Z. alert hooks wired to #oncall if auto-disable triggers.
zhen: thanks. i'll craft the RFC addendum with DSL grammar and a prototype compiler tomorrow. will ping when PR is up.
leo: thanks, excited.
anya: appreciate the pragmatic constraints. we'll iterate on presets first to reduce operator footguns.
